result.paraphrase: Over the past decades, learning technologies have advanced significantly, allowing learners to participate in learning activities anywhere. In Tanzania, mobile internet penetration increased from 2 million users in 2011 to 23 million in 2017. However, adopting mobile-based learning (M-learning) for visually impaired students remains a major challenge because most e-learning content assumes sighted learners and relies heavily on visual material. As a result, visually impaired students in higher learning institutions (HLIs) encounter problems such as technical knowledge gaps, limited access to online content, and even university dropout. This study aimed to assess awareness and use of existing mobile assistive technologies for visual impairment, as well as the remaining challenges visually impaired students face when using smartphones to access m-learning content from HLIs in Tanzania. The research used an observational and contextual inquiry design at three major HLIs. Results showed that 67% of respondents lacked knowledge of m-learning assistive technologies and related barriers. In addition, knowledge, accessibility of assistive technology, and affordability can limit the adoption of m-learning in higher learning institutions.
